svg.text: FashionSearch Architecture — Mapped to Kreuzberger et al.'s MLOps Framework
Fashion visual search — two pretrained models imported, not trained; a single-platform Databricks pipeline
A · Product Initiation Zone — config.yaml, one file
and wants to buy the jacket in it.
B · Data Engineering Zone — Databricks Unity Catalog (serverless)
data preprocessing — serverless compute, no GPU
Requirements for the feature engineering pipeline
Split by product_id, never by row.
C · ML Experimentation Zone — no training happens here
model engineering — import, validate, export. Both checkpoints arrive already trained.
ML metadata store — one MLflow run per gate evaluation; slice_metrics.json and gate_report.json logged
Model training computation infrastructure — Databricks serverless CPU. No GPU: the models are already trained.
Repository · GitHub saaspace2/fashionsearch · one repo: code, config, tests · a push here triggers the CI/CD component
only a human moves the rest, and every move is logged with a name.
D · Automated ML Workflow Pipeline — runs once a model holds @production
one row per slice per version
Databricks Model Serving — embeds ONE query image per request.
The catalogue is pre-embedded in batch, so the two million products
are never encoded online. That asymmetry is what makes it affordable.
Feedback Loop — enables continuous training, retraining and improvement
reformulation rate, index staleness, p95 latency.
Reported per category, never only on average: one category collapsing
is invisible in the mean, and is usually the first sign of a regression.
A clicked result is a new positive pair, labelled by a human who had every
incentive to get it right. Results shown above it and skipped are hard
negatives — worth far more than random ones the model solved weeks ago.
Both land in the next train_pairs version, whose update triggers the
pipeline again. Zero labelling cost, real query distribution.
Where this differs from the framework
Kreuzberger's Zone C normally contains model training. Here it does not — both models arrive already trained from
Hugging Face, so the zone runs import, validation and export only. Everything else the framework asks for is still
present: config-driven design, versioned features, a frozen holdout, per-slice validation, a registry with aliases,
a promotion gate and a feedback loop. That is the point. The value was never in the training step.
FIGURE — adapted. End-to-end architecture of the FashionSearch visual search pipeline, mapped onto Kreuzberger, Kühl & Hirschl's end-to-end MLOps
architecture and workflow (Fig. 4, Machine Learning Operations (MLOps): Overview, Definition, and Architecture, IEEE Access, 2023).
